messages.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 15 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about a thousand words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, what brought you to HD recently?

Well, I'm interested in buying a solo miner. To maximize my chances of winning uh, Bitcoin lottery and not, uh, pay too much for electricity. And, uh, maximize my chances at an efficient, uh, hash rate that, um, with chips that are um, cutting edge in the latest technology.

Got it — solo miner, lottery odds, watch the power bill, and you want current-gen silicon. That's a clear picture.

I saw you were looking at the Nexus Dual Pack — let me pull that up. Actually — one sec, let me grab the right page. You added the Nexus Dual Pack to your cart at $999 — what made that one stand out to you?

Well, uh, it's a bundle. So it's already giving me a a savings. Secondly, it's the latest, uh, most efficient chips available. It's actually preorder. They're not even out yet. They offer, um, an adequate amount of hash rate towards power consumption. Um, I'd I'd like it to be, uh, you know, twelve instead of ten. But ten is sufficient, uh, given that it's quiet and comes in a sleek um, three d printed uh, housing or stand, if you will.

That's a really specific picture — preorder, latest chips, 10 TH/s, quiet, the 3D-printed housing. You clearly did homework on this one.

You said "latest, most efficient chips available, not even out yet" — where did you learn about it? Like, what got you onto the Nexus specifically?

Hey, Started out with some uh, loud and noisy They were, uh, I I believe it was a Wow. It was a nerd q x of solo minor at six t h and sixteen point five j t h. They were a bit expensive and, uh, loud and noisy. I I I realized I had made the poor choice. And so, uh, afterwards, I thought, well, let me get something uh, with the ASIC chips, and I looking at a six zero two or a seven zero two. Um, and then I stumbled upon, uh, through lots of questions, I was asking um, what alternatives are available And, um, I didn't wanna paint myself into a corner with technology that's on its way out. Uh, so I was, uh, searching using AI comparing the nerd octane and the big ax gamma plus plus. When, uh, it offered the bleeding edge helium deploy Nexus s one as an alternative. That's when I found out about the BM thirteen seventy six ASIC chips. And the newer Antminer s twenty three generation, which alerted me to uh, you know, that's when I found out about this, uh, s one. And I'm I. I'd like to buy one.

Wow — okay, that's a fantastic story. So you went from a loud NerdQaxe, looked at 602/702s, then AI-comparison-shopped Gamma++ vs NerdOctane, and the AI itself surfaced the Nexus S1 with the BM1376. That's a journey.

You said you "made the poor choice" with the NerdQaxe — what was the moment you realized that?

Well, then they delivered them, and I didn't I didn't really open them or try and use them. I don't know. I guess I was like, what did I do? I think I spent too much money on something. Um, and I just asked a quick question. Did I overspend? On something that, uh, there's a better option? And they quickly told me there's a lot of options out there. And I and I realized it was, um, impulse buy. And I do enjoy the retail therapy. But uh, I I don't enjoy the cognitive dissonance. So I had to return them without trying them out.

Oh man — "retail therapy but not the cognitive dissonance." That's such an honest way to put it. You returned them unopened.

How did the return go?

Um, it's uneventful. They they they wanna check on to see that, uh, they were in the same condition as they shipped, which, uh, they they have they weren't even opened. And so I'm just waiting for that to Um, you finalized. I've got, uh, on good information that, uh, there should be no problems. And they even gave me fifteen dollar credit for inquiring about any delay. So I'd say pretty good.

That's great to hear — uneventful return, $15 credit for the delay inquiry. Honestly that's the kind of thing we never know if it actually lands well, so thank you for telling me.

You said earlier you didn't want to "paint yourself into a corner with technology that's on its way out" — say more about that. What does that look like in your head?

Okay. Well, the ASICs technology in the the, uh, I guess, what is it called? The gamma um, the gamma plus plus, it's still efficient, uh, more efficient than the ASICs chips in the Stelloplex or the um,
Mhm —

the chips that are used for um, what is it called? The the biddax EX um, versions, uh, the seven zero two or the the super hex. What are those chips there? The eighteen thirteen seventy a six chips? And the thirteen sixty eight ASIC chips. Uh, are older. They might be the gamma but there's they're replacing the What is it? Uh, the thirteen sixty eight chips. Right? So um, those those have been around for a while. And the s one is using more efficient chips.

Got it — so you've got real chip-level fluency. The 1368s feel like yesterday's silicon, the Gamma++ is still efficient but aging, and the BM1376 in the S1 is what's next.

Here's where I want to push you a bit. The S1 is preorder — nobody has one in hand yet. Meanwhile a NerdQaxe at 6 TH/s exists, ships today, and the math on $/TH is actually pretty competitive. What makes you willing to wait for silicon that hasn't shipped versus just buying what's in stock?
Uh, new technology. Our newest. Bleeding edge.

"Bleeding edge." That's the word.

But why does bleeding edge matter to YOU? Like — you're solo mining, the odds of hitting a block are basically the same whether you're at 6 TH/s or 10 TH/s. So what's pulling you toward the newest?
Continuity.
Continuity — say more about that.
What what technology is gonna last longer and have longer support?

Ahh — okay, that's a really different answer than I expected. It's not about hashrate or lottery odds, it's about how long the thing stays relevant before it becomes e-waste. Support, firmware, the ecosystem still caring about your chip a year or two from now.

Have you been burned by that before? Like, owned a piece of tech that got abandoned?
No. It hasn't happened to me.

Fair enough — so it's more of a forward-looking worry than something you've actually lived through. Where did the worry come from then? Did you read something, see a thread, hear someone talk about older chips losing support?

No. Uh, it's I just made it up. I just, uh, chips are are only good for so long. They have, uh, a shelf life like any other technology. And I wouldn't say it's a worry. Rather it's just, um, you know, obsolescence

Got it — not a worry, just obsolescence as a basic fact of tech. You want to be on the front end of the curve, not the back. That makes sense.

Let me show you something — the Nexus isn't the only option in that space. Want to see what else is in the lineup? I just pulled up the Canaan Avalon Q — have you looked at this one?
I have. I'm not interested.
Why not?
I like the s one.

Fair — you know what you want.

Let me ask about the bundle specifically though. The N. Dual Pack is the S1 paired with the L1 — Litecoin/Dogecoin side. The S1 alone would be cheaper. What made you go for the dual pack instead of just the S1?
I like buying bundles.
Why bundles?
Savings.
Got it — straight savings play. Do you actually care about mining Litecoin and Doge, or is the L1 kind of a bonus you'll figure out later?
Absolutely. I I I wanna mine, like, Conan George.

Nice — so it's not a throwaway bonus, you actually want both sides running. Good.

Let me pull the bundle page up so we're looking at the same thing. You added it to cart back on the 25th but didn't check out — what stopped you?
Can you repeat that? Couldn't hear you.
Sure — you added the Nexus Dual Pack to your cart on the 25th, but didn't actually complete the purchase. What stopped you?
Well, I tried several codes to get a discount. None of them worked and the one that I did said it didn't apply to the nexus.

Ahhh — okay, that's huge. So you were ready to buy, you went hunting for a discount code, tried several, and the one that DID work was excluded from the Nexus. That's the friction point.

Where were you finding those codes? Like, where did you go looking?
Well, those are my secrets. No. I I just searched online
Ha, fair — trade secrets. So you Googled around for HD discount codes. And when the working code excluded the Nexus, what went through your head?
I'll think about it in the morning.

"Think about it in the morning" — and here we are. So the cart's been sitting since the 25th.

What would it take to get you off the fence? Like, if you woke up tomorrow and pulled the trigger, what would have to be true?
I don't know. Uh, discount code, they worked, and then applied towards what's in my cart.

Crystal clear — a working code that actually applies to the Nexus. That's the unlock.

One last thing I'm curious about. You mentioned earlier you used AI to comparison-shop the Gamma++ and NerdOctane before the Nexus surfaced. Beyond HD, were you looking at other stores too? Like, did the AI point you anywhere else?
Yes. It's several stores, but not for the s one. Well, you pointed me at several vendors for all the different models I was looking at. Sure.

Got it — so for the older models, lots of vendors, but for the S1 specifically, HD is the only game in town. That's why you're here.

Which other vendors came up for the older models? Just curious which ones the AI surfaced.
I don't recall It's unimportant. What's more important is what I'm looking after what I'm looking for. And so none.

Fair — and honestly, that's a clean answer in itself. The S1 is what you want, HD is who has it, the only thing in the way is a working discount code. That's the whole story.

This has been really helpful — before we wrap, is there anything we didn't cover that you wish we had? Anything you'd want the HD founders to actually hear?
Make good products.

Ha — short and to the point. Make good products. I'll pass it along, word for word.

Sincerely, thank you — this was genuinely useful. The chip-rotation thinking, the "retail therapy without the cognitive dissonance" line, and the discount-code friction on the Nexus — all of that is going straight to the team. Your $75 code will land in your inbox shortly.

Take care.
